attempted_counterexamples.scenario: Add a `GET /healthz` branch to the plain http.createServer callback and assume it can coexist with Engine.IO without touching /socket.io.
attempted_counterexamples.assumption: plan.md:74-78 — the plain handler sees every request, so a branch there serves /healthz and 'anything else' keeps the existing text for Engine.IO paths.
attempted_counterexamples.evidence: node_modules/engine.io/build/server.js:674-686 (attach caches and removes the existing 'request' listeners, then re-dispatches only non-matching paths to them); local run of the plan's exact handler shape returned ["/healthz",200,"{\"ok\":true,\"workers\":7}"],["/socket.io/?EIO=4&transport=polling",200,"0{\"sid\"..."], handler order ["plain:/healthz"] — the plain handler was never called for /socket.io.
attempted_counterexamples.observed: The /healthz branch works and Engine.IO polling is unaffected; the plain handler is in fact only ever reached for non-/socket.io paths, which also means the existing 'socket.io server' text is already dead code for Engine.IO.
attempted_counterexamples.uncertainty: Verified on the installed socket.io 4.8.4 / engine.io build only; an upgrade could change the listener-replay behaviour.

attempted_counterexamples.scenario: Join the 9 fleet nodes to Prometheus target health by private IP, on a fleet the evidence says is 9/9 up.
attempted_counterexamples.assumption: plan.md:104-105 + deploy/FLEET.md:26 ('node_exporter on all 9') — every node has a target whose identity is its private IP, so a healthy fleet yields 9 green rows.
attempted_counterexamples.evidence: evidence-fleet.txt:9 'host.docker.internal:9100 up' is the only target for db-mon-1 (deploy/FLEET.md:12 says db-mon-1 is 10.20.0.30); the other eight targets are rendered as '<private-ip>:9100'. Nothing in the plan strips ':9100' before matching.
attempted_counterexamples.observed: db-mon-1 (10.20.0.30) has no target whose name is an IP, so the plan's 'absent -> red "no node_exporter target"' fires on a fully healthy fleet. If the comparison is literal equality against '10.20.0.41:9100', all 9 rows go red.
attempted_counterexamples.uncertainty: The exact label used is /api/v1/targets' labels.instance (inferred from the evidence rendering, not read from the live API); if the join instead uses a scrape-config label or stripped instance, only the host.docker.internal case survives.

attempted_counterexamples.scenario: Bound a hung-NFS statfs with a 1200 ms race so that GET /api/admin/health has bounded latency and the page cannot hang or amplify load.
attempted_counterexamples.assumption: plan.md:62,67,69,156-157 — 'the request thread may stay until the mount recovers' implies one stuck thread and a request that returns red, i.e. contained damage.
attempted_counterexamples.evidence: 4 blocking fs.promises calls (FIFO reads) starved an unrelated fs.promises.stat for >2 s on Node v24.21.0 with UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE unset (default 4): output 'STAT-BLOCKED-2s at 2305'. server/admin/api.js:5 imports node:fs/promises and calls await fs.stat/fs.readFile/fs.open throughout (e.g. api.js:160, api.js:730).
attempted_counterexamples.observed: Node has no per-request thread: a timed-out statfs keeps one of the 4 shared libuv threads until the mount recovers. Four statfs that outlive their 1200 ms budget (4 concurrent cold-cache tabs, or 4 refreshes at the 5 s cache interval) stall every fs operation in the web process — account list, image streaming, catalog — while the health probes (loopback IPs, no DNS) keep answering green.
attempted_counterexamples.uncertainty: The FIFO test proves threadpool sharing, not that statfs itself blocks; the blocking behaviour is the plan's own claim (plan.md:156) and untested against the real hard mount.

attempted_counterexamples.scenario: Report S4 health as 'configured + heartbeat < 10 min' from the web process on session-1.
attempted_counterexamples.assumption: plan.md:47 — an S4 run heartbeat of some kind is readable by the panel, so a working mirror can reach green.
attempted_counterexamples.evidence: grep of server/ for heartbeat/lastRun/s4 status returns nothing; the only S4 artifact is a per-account marker python/s4_upload.py:138 (account / 'Scan' / 's4-complete.json'); FLEET.md:34-36 puts S4 config on session/download nodes, and FLEET.md:29 lists no S4 key for session-1.
attempted_counterexamples.observed: No producer of a <10 min S4 heartbeat exists. With S4 configured the check is permanently yellow (stale heartbeat), and with S4 unconfigured it is yellow by the plan's own rule — so 'S4 yellow' in acceptance step 3 (plan.md:144) is guaranteed regardless of mirror health.
attempted_counterexamples.uncertainty: A cron on a download node could write a marker outside the repo; I did not inspect the live hosts.

attempted_counterexamples.scenario: Place GET /health immediately after router.use(requireSession) in server/admin/api.js so unauthenticated callers get 401 and errors keep the JSON shape.
attempted_counterexamples.assumption: map.md:11 and plan.md:88-98 — placement after line 217 and before the error handler at 743 is required for both behaviours.
attempted_counterexamples.evidence: server/admin/api.js:177 requireSession returns res.status(401).json({ok:false,error:'unauthorized'}); :217 applies it; :743 router.use((error,_req,res,_next)=>{...res.status(500).json(...)}). api.js:37-39 asyncRoute forwards rejections to next.
attempted_counterexamples.observed: Both behaviours hold at that placement: 401 shape for anon, 500 JSON for a rejection. A route registered after 743 would fall through to Express's default HTML error handler.
attempted_counterexamples.uncertainty: None material; Express 5 middleware ordering is as documented.

reason: Architecture and route placement are sound; the /healthz branch was verified against engine.io. But the node join is wrong for the fleet it must describe (db-mon-1 is host.docker.internal), so a healthy fleet shows a red node; statfs is not bounded by a race, it leaks one of four libuv threads per refresh and can freeze the panel; S4 and Redis have no data source/credential path, so both sit yellow forever.
